extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers / observational scientists (Royal Society readers, astronomers, botanists, instrument-makers)
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and reporting detailed empirical observations and apparatus descriptions for natural-philosophy/astronomical/biological phenomena, including instrumentation, measurements, locations, and references needed for reproducibility and comparison with prior work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify instruments and their exact specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the instruments used and their dimensions or identifying characteristics (e.g., tube lengths, micrometer type, pendulum clock).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the text: 'two tubes; the one 1964- inches long... the other only 103-i- inches long, with my own micrometer'; 'Time by the Pendulum Clock'. Always name the instrument, give measurable dimensions or model-like identifiers, and indicate which instrument was used for which measurements. Omitting instrument specs reduces reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record raw observed times and corrected times
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide both the initially observed times and the times after applying corrections (e.g., for altitude, meridian line), with clear labels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text shows columns 'Time by the Pend. Clock.' and 'Corrected Time.' and notes 'The times corrected by observed altitudes.' Present both sets and state the correction method so readers can evaluate the corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: State measurement procedures and step-by-step methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe exactly how measurements were taken (order of actions, simultaneous measurements by different observers, which micrometer/telescope was used at which phase).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The eclipse report describes using two tubes simultaneously, with Halley and the author taking complementary measures. Give procedural sequence (who measured what, when), so others understand the method and potential sources of discrepancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide numerical results with units, durations, and difference/uncertainty entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Give numeric measurements with units (h/m/s, degrees, minutes), durations, quantities, and report differences or uncertainties numerically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Beginning ... 4 31 42', 'The duration 1 53 16', 'The quantity 6° 5''', and a 'Differences, min.' column. Include difference columns or uncertainty annotations to make precision and agreement between measures explicit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe apparatus construction in reproducible detail
rubrics_metrics.description: When inventing or modifying instruments, give materials, dimensions, assembly steps, and how parts interact so others can reconstruct the device (e.g., hygroscope construction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The hygroscope description lists board sizes, brass plate with teeth, pinion, axis, index, fastening points (aaaa), and expected motion (a quarter inch gap = one revolution). Provide similar level of detail, diagrams, and notes on alternative materials (poplar vs. deal). Anti-pattern: vague description without dimensions or function of parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include figures/plate references for visual evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference and include figures/plates for anatomical, instrumental, or observational evidence (e.g., 'fig. 6, pi. 9', 'fig. 8, AB').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article repeatedly cites figures/plates tied to descriptions. Always provide numbered figures and link textual descriptions to them so readers can see morphology or instrument layouts; without figures some morphological claims are hard to assess.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report observer identities and roles
rubrics_metrics.description: State who made which observations, assisted, or computed (e.g., names of observers and their contributions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The eclipse account names Mr. Halley, Lord Viscount Brouncker, Mr. Townly and assigns specific tasks. Listing observers and roles helps assess expertise, possible biases, and validate independent replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give geographic location and orientation data
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide observation location details (town, latitude, longitude with reference meridian) and local conditions relevant to measurements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Observed at Dantzic', 'Lat. 53° 44', and 'Long. 0 min. West of the Meridian of London.' Include local meridian/clock references and environmental notes (clouds, visibility) that affect interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare observations to established tables and prior literature
rubrics_metrics.description: State which reference tables or prior works were used for calculation/verification (e.g., Rudolphine Tables) and compare results to earlier authors or editions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text cites 'Calcul. by the Rudolphine Table' and discusses Dr. Grew, Malpighi, and prior Transactions numbers. Explicit comparison allows evaluating consistency and pointing out deviations; always cite the exact reference/version used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe specimens and observed phenomena with precise morphological detail
rubrics_metrics.description: For biological or material observations, describe form, color, proportions, behavior, and relevant measurements (e.g., beetle horns, vine vessels, 'little eels' in wine).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The beetle is described as 'dark shining brown, with a huge pair of horns... shaped and branched exactly like a stag's'. Such careful morphological description plus figure references is required to identify specimens; avoid vague adjectives without measurements or comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document treatments and experimental manipulations
rubrics_metrics.description: When samples are manipulated (e.g., wine vessel fumigation, cloth dipped in brimstone, water storage), record the treatment steps and timing so effects can be evaluated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'a coarse linen cloth dipped in melted brimstone and kindled had been hung over the vessel before it was filled.' Include when treatments occurred relative to observation and any measures of initial conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give anatomical/structural interpretations tied to microscopy/figures and acknowledge alternative readings
rubrics_metrics.description: When interpreting microstructure (vessels, pores, valves), explicitly describe what was seen, how it was seen, and reference alternate interpretations or prior authors' terms (e.g., Leewenhoeck vs. Grew terminology).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author describes three sorts of vessels, valves, globules, and compares to Dr. Grew's figures and nomenclature. State observational basis (slices, magnification) and discuss how different terminologies map; note where disagreement or ambiguity exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide tabulated measurement series and clearly label columns/metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Present measurements in tables with clear column headings (e.g., phase measures AB/CD, instrument identifiers PL/IC/AZ) and explain abbreviations or coding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The eclipse tables show columns for 'Measures of the Phases' with AB, CD entries and instrument codes (PL, IC, AZ). Always define codes, units, and any conversion factors used so tables are interpretable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note observational conditions and anomalies impacting instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: Document transient events or anomalies (e.g., lightning affecting compasses, clouds during eclipse) and how they impacted readings or instrument behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: compass cards turned after thunder, 'The sun then hid by clouds'. Report such incidents, what was observed, and any measures taken (e.g., retaking measurements) so readers can factor them into data trustworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite prior sections and serial publication identifiers for traceability
rubrics_metrics.description: When referring to previously published material in the same serial (e.g., 'N° 127, p. 653', 'N° 27 of your Transactions'), give issue numbers and page references for readers to locate the cited items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article repeatedly cites Transactions numbers and page numbers. Use such precise citations to allow readers to follow arguments, examine referenced figures, and verify claims.
